paragraphs.text: Brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia. Its features include short-trunk short stature and normal intelligence. Radiographs show platyspondyly or rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral spaces, along with variable, generally mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones (Ahmad et al., 1998; Miyake et al., 2012). Miyake et al. (2012) concluded that PAPSS2 mutations produce a skeletal dysplasia family with a gradation of phenotypes ranging from brachyolmia to spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large, inbred, 8-generation kindred from a remote area of Pakistan with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD). They evaluated 16 affected individuals (11 males and 5 females). Clinical findings included short stature evident at birth, short bowed lower limbs, mild brachydactyly, kyphoscoliosis, an abnormal gait, enlarged knee joints, precocious osteoarthropathy, and normal intelligence. Radiographs showed delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees and platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces. There were diffuse early osteoarthritic changes, mainly in the spine and hands, and mild brachydactyly. Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen mostly at the hips and knees.

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) described 6 patients with autosomal recessive brachyolmia: 3 affected members of a Turkish family, 2 Japanese patients, and 1 Korean patient. The patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood, with normal intelligence and facies. Radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of rib cartilages, short femoral neck, and mildly shortened metacarpals. Spinal changes were very similar among the 6 patients, whereas epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones were variable.

paragraphs.text: In 3 affected members of a Turkish family with autosomal recessive brachyolmia, Miyake et al. (2012) used exon capture followed by next-generation sequencing to identify a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the PAPSS2 gene (c.337_338insG; p.A113GfsX18). They then studied 3 additional patients (2 Japanese and 1 Korean) with a similar brachyolmia phenotype and found PAPSS2 mutations in all 3. One patient was homozygous for a splice site mutation (IVS3+2delT). The second was compound heterozygous for 2 loss-of-function mutations (c.616-634del19, p.V206SfsX9 and c.1309-1310delAG, p.R437GfsX19). The third was compound heterozygous for 2 other loss-of-function mutations (c.480_481insCGTA, p.K161RfsX6 and c.661delA, p.I221SfsX40).
